## 固定收益開盤主論述

7月23日，美國公債延續跌勢。兩艘沙烏地阿拉伯油輪遇襲，為中東衝突開闢第2條活躍的航運戰線，布蘭特原油因而升破每桶$100，聯準會在7月會議升息的可能性也隨之上升。政策敏感天期領跌，2年期與5年期殖利率均上升4.9個基點，分別至4.348%與4.453%；10年期上升3.8個基點至4.694%，30年期則上升1.5個基點至5.161%。殖利率曲線呈熊市趨平，2s10s縮窄1.1個基點至34.6個基點，2s30s縮窄3.4個基點至81.3個基點。

本交易時段同時反映兩項力量：潛在能源衝擊擴大，以及美國勞動市場仍讓聯準會有空間聚焦通膨。截至7月18日當週，初領失業救濟人數減少2.2萬人至18.7萬人，創1969年以來最低，遠低於21萬人的預測中位數。交換市場估計，7月28至29日會議升息25個基點的機率約為35%，高於一週前的約10%，並已完全反映最遲9月升息一次。

美國公債的變動組成顯示，單靠通膨補償不足以解釋這波調整。10年期實質殖利率上升5.7個基點至2.424%，10年期損益兩平通膨率卻下降1.9個基點至2.27%。油價改變了近期政策盤算，但在勞動數據仍穩健、經濟持續吸收龐大投資支出的情況下，投資人也要求更高的通膨調整後報酬。前端領跌、曲線趨平，顯示邊際政策調整集中於政策敏感天期；30年期殖利率持續守在5%以上，則顯示財政與企業債供給的另一重壓力仍在。

原油是當日最關鍵的衝擊。布蘭特原油上漲6.97%至$100.63，一週累計上漲19.47%，一個月累計上漲29.18%；WTI上漲6.18%至$92.20。胡塞武裝表示以飛彈與無人機攻擊紅海上的兩艘沙烏地阿拉伯油輪；在此之前，荷莫茲海峽長達數月的干擾已妨礙波斯灣航運。這次攻擊威脅到沙烏地阿拉伯為維持出口所仰賴的替代航線，而華盛頓與德黑蘭仍不願恢復談判，美國總統川普並揚言發動更大規模攻擊。

風險資產未能為利率市場的跌勢提供多少緩衝。標普500指數下跌1.21%，那斯達克100指數下跌1.87%，VIX則上升12.38%至18.70。Alphabet上調資本支出計畫，加上Tesla公布財報，使市場重新評估AI投資；與此同時，油價及殖利率上升也壓抑估值。美元指數上漲0.29%，黃金則下跌2.29%至$4,051.80，反映實質殖利率上升與潛在政策緊縮的影響壓過地緣政治避險需求。投資等級與高收益債券基金均下跌約0.4%，一檔新興市場債券基金下跌0.59%，顯示交易型信用資產承壓，但尚不足以證明利差全面失守。

油價引發的重新定價遍及全球。歐洲央行將存款利率維持在2.25%，但總裁拉加德透露，部分官員曾考慮立即升息，並保留9月採取行動的可能性。德國10年期公債殖利率觸及15年高點，收盤約為3.19%。土耳其同樣維持利率不變，但在官員觀察能源成本是否會中斷通膨降溫之際，有效融資成本仍高達40%。各國的共同變化並非同步緊縮，而是在國內通膨、成長與匯率條件各異之下，決策者已更難忽視輸入型能源壓力。

## 油價把聯準會決策時點推向眼前

沙烏地阿拉伯油輪遇襲，使紅海的潛在威脅成為實際干擾。胡塞武裝表示，為封鎖沙烏地阿拉伯港口，已向兩艘船發射飛彈與無人機；一名油輪船長則通報，船隻在沙烏地阿拉伯沿岸Al Shuqaiq西南方遭到攻擊。衝突如今同時涵蓋波斯灣主要出口通道荷莫茲海峽，以及連接蘇伊士運河的紅海航線。

第2條戰線之所以重要，是因為替代基礎設施與航運路線原本限制了荷莫茲交通受阻的影響。沙烏地阿拉伯貨物在紅海遭受干擾，降低了這層緩衝的可靠性；即使尚未出現實際產量損失，運費、保險與交付時程的風險也已上升。全球庫存先前已因數月衝突而下降，布蘭特原油收在$100.63，近兩個月來首次收於$100以上。

情勢升級也增添了更明確的美國政策層面。川普表示，若胡塞武裝進一步攻擊，將追究伊朗責任，且他已接近決定是否發動規模大得多的攻擊。華盛頓與德黑蘭均未表示談判即將展開。因此，美國公債市場定價的不只是當日油價跳升，也包括衝突延長或擴大、使能源成本長期高到足以影響商品、服務、工資與通膨預期的風險。

市場定價迅速轉向聯準會可能立即採取行動。與會議日期連結的交換合約顯示，7月升息的機率接近35%，高於一週前的約10%，而市場已完全反映最遲9月升息25個基點。距離會議如此接近時出現這麼大的變化格外值得注意，尤其聯準會主席凱文・沃許提供的事前指引少於前幾任主席。由於決策方向並未獲得明確預告，投資人更願意同時為升息與按兵不動保留機率。

部分利率投資人認為，市場對7月升息的定價過於進取。道明證券策略師Gennadiy Goldberg認為，聯準會在恢復升息前，可能希望再觀察數月的核心通膨證據，儘管今年稍後升息的風險已相當顯著。這項區別很重要：油價確實提高了重新緊縮的機率，但市場尚未取得能源漲價已擴散至基礎通膨的證據。

不過，初領失業救濟數據也削弱了把能源衝擊視為唯一考量的理由。初次申請人數由20.9萬人降至18.7萬人，低於21萬人的預測，顯示裁員仍異常有限。勞動市場幾乎看不到解僱壓力，使決策者有更大空間回應未來通膨壓力，而不會立刻與其就業職責產生明顯衝突。

這份報告也不是毫無疑義的經濟加速訊號。最新月度就業數據顯示，一些勞工正在退出勞動市場；這種情況可能降低申領失業救濟人數，卻不代表勞動需求轉強。即便有這項保留，當週數據仍未顯示足以迫使聯準會淡化新一輪能源衝擊的廣泛惡化。

房市則更清楚呈現市場殖利率偏高所帶來的抑制作用。30年期固定房貸平均利率連續第3週上升，由6.55%升至6.58%，但仍低於一年前的6.74%。脆弱的停火協議破裂後，美國公債殖利率反彈並帶動房貸利率上升，逆轉了先前開始支撐住房需求的部分融資成本改善。

當日曲線變化反映潛在通膨與既有緊縮作用之間的拉鋸。2年期殖利率升至4.348%，一週上升20.6個基點；10年期升至4.694%，同期上升14個基點。30年期殖利率當日漲幅較小，但一個月已上升21.2個基點。近期政策風險帶動最新一波曲線趨平；期限殖利率與實質殖利率維持高檔，則使長天期融資即使沒有同等幅度的單日變動，依然受到明顯限制。

實質殖利率的升幅尤其值得注意。由於損益兩平通膨率下降，10年期TIPS殖利率上升5.7個基點，幅度超過名目10年期殖利率的3.8個基點升幅。這種組合並不否定油價是催化因素，而是顯示市場面對衝擊時，部分反應是提高預期政策與實質利率負擔，而非單純增加通膨補償。

重新定價期間，美國公債交易活動同步擴大。FINRA記錄的面額交易量達$1.158兆，共411,593筆，總交易活動較前一日增加12.2%。名目附息債券成交量增加16.4%至$9,126億。剩餘期限超過7年、但不超過10年的債券交易量增加33.7%至$1,886億，5至7年期區段則增加33.6%至$779億。這些數據顯示，承受重新定價的天期出現異常活躍的雙向交易，但無法判斷客戶是淨買方或淨賣方。

交易時段稍晚的貿易政策行動又增添一項潛在價格風險。美國在完成強迫勞動調查後，對約60個經濟體的進口品課徵10%至12.5%關稅，日本與南韓適用區間上限；燃料、食品與肥料獲得豁免。這些豁免限制了關稅與當日能源衝擊最直接的重疊，但更廣泛的關稅壁壘仍構成另一條可能透過投入成本與供應鏈影響通膨前景的管道。

## 歐洲暫停升息，但未關閉後續行動空間

歐洲央行一致決議將存款利率維持在2.25%、主要再融資利率維持在2.40%，邊際放款利率維持在2.65%。資產購買計畫與疫情緊急購債計畫的投資組合繼續縮減，不再將到期本金再投資。這項決策接續6月升息25個基點，並維持逐次會議決定的方式，讓官員評估能源衝擊將持續多久、擴散多廣。

維持利率不變並非中性訊號。拉加德表示，部分管理委員曾詢問歐洲央行是否應立即升息。她認為目前設定適當，可讓官員等待後續資訊，但同時強調通膨風險偏向上行；能源價格若長期上升，便更可能傳導至其他價格與工資。

官員尤其關切油價與天然氣價格的交互影響。拉加德舉行記者會期間，布蘭特原油升破$100；歐洲天然氣價格也在庫存偏低的背景下上漲。歐洲央行已要求工作人員為9月會議進行更詳盡的能源分析，屆時決策者將取得新預測、額外兩個月的通膨數據及更多企業調查。

近期通膨證據仍相對溫和。6月整體通膨率由5月的3.2%降至2.8%，基礎價格漲幅也持續受控。拉加德表示，目前尚未看到二輪效應跡象。不過，歐洲央行仍預期，累積的能源漲幅及其向食品、商品與服務的傳導，將使通膨在2027年上半年持續遠高於目標。

這種組合說明了為何9月成為焦點，而歐洲央行沒有在7月行動。熟悉討論內容的官員表示，除非通膨前景顯著改善，否則可能還需要再升息25個基點；但他們也強調尚未作成決定，和平協議或更嚴重的經濟下滑都可能改變評估。

德國公債已先行反映大部分風險。10年期德債殖利率一度升至3.21%，為2011年以來最高，終場約收在3.19%，上升2個基點。交換市場認為9月升息幾近確定，且接近完全反映年底前再升息一次。市場對本次決策反應有限，顯示維持利率不變已在預期之中，投資人更關注能源與附帶條件的9月政策路徑。

供給則是支撐歐洲殖利率上升的另一項獨立因素。德國的國防與基礎建設計畫需要大舉舉債，相關支出也可能支撐經濟活動，進而強化維持限制性政策的理由。英國10年期公債殖利率約為5.09%，市場預期英格蘭銀行年底前將升息兩次，並於2027年年中前再升息一次。歐洲與英國利率已再次與原油呈現強烈的同向關係，儘管各國央行面對的通膨及成長條件並不相同。

土耳其再次選擇維持限制性政策。央行連續第4次會議把1週期附買回利率維持在37%，符合全部20名經濟學家的預測，並將隔夜放款利率維持在40%。伊朗戰爭爆發以來，隔夜利率一直是實際融資成本，因此政策利率不變並不像表面上那麼寬鬆。

土耳其貨幣政策委員會表示，地緣政治不確定性再起並推高能源價格，7月基礎通膨趨勢將暫時上升。6月年通膨率已降至32.1%，是衝突爆發後首次減速，但央行希望先評估7月數據與戰況，再調整利率路徑。決策公布後，里拉變動不大，約為1美元兌47.23里拉。

市場對政策前景的看法仍然分歧：一方面需要維持通膨降溫，另一方面，下一步最終仍可能轉向寬鬆。BBVA策略師Tufan Comert預期，秋季前有效融資成本不會明顯下降；但若外部風險消退，且通膨在預期於7月回升後再度降溫，他認為下一步仍較可能是寬鬆。彭博經濟研究預期37%的政策利率將維持至年底，並預測12月通膨率為29.5%，高於央行預估的26%。

墨西哥的通膨問題較不急迫，但改善程度仍不足以支持再次降息。7月上半月整體通膨率由6月的3.18%降至3.1%，符合預測並創2020年以來最低。核心通膨率由3.94%微升至3.95%，略高於預期；服務通膨則降至4.36%。

墨西哥央行6月底一致決議將政策利率維持在6.50%，並表示保持這項設定是適當之舉。最新整體通膨下滑支持暫停降息，但核心與服務價格黏著，並不利於立即降息。央行預期第4季整體與核心通膨率均為3.5%，並於2027年第2季回到3%目標，同時仍判斷這條路徑面臨的風險偏向上行。

## 中國與日本的亞洲長天期債市走勢分歧

中國公債逆全球跌勢上漲。成長轉弱、股市下跌，加上市場預期將有更多貨幣支持，使投資人重新增持長天期債券。30年期公債期貨升至去年11月以來最高，未平倉合約單日增加15%至紀錄高點。現券30年期殖利率已由3月高點2.39%降至2.21%，10年期殖利率則下降2個基點至1.73%。

這波漲勢發生在第2季成長弱於預期之後，市場並猜測部分銀行可能下調存款利率。投資人也預期中共中央政治局會議可能推出刺激措施。這些國內預期的影響，壓過了推高美國、歐洲及英國殖利率的全球通膨衝擊。

標售需求進一步強化漲勢。10年期公債標售的投標金額達發行額7.41倍，是彭博自2004年開始統計以來最高。流動性充裕、股市波動及地緣政治不確定性均支撐需求；不過，這波漲勢能否延續，可能取決於10年期殖利率能否跌破1.70%，而不引發中國人民銀行疑慮。

日本面對相反局勢：輸入型能源壓力、異常疲弱的日圓，以及已開始退出寬鬆的央行。日圓一度跌至1美元兌163.99日圓，為40年來最低。彭博調查顯示，52名經濟學家中有50%預期日本央行下次升息在12月，40%預期在10月；市場則估計10月前升息的機率為83%。

即使在最新通膨數據公布前，經濟學家也愈來愈願意接受較早升息。37%認為9月是最早可能緊縮的時點，高於6月會議後的23%。同時，59%把首相高市早苗偏好貨幣支持視為加速政策正常化的障礙，82%預期升息步調約為每6個月一次。

日本時間週五清晨公布的新通膨數據強化了今年稍後進一步緊縮的理由，但數據是在美國交易時段收盤後才發布。6月不含生鮮食品的CPI年增1.6%，符合預測中位數，並為3個月來首次加速。整體通膨，以及不含生鮮食品與能源的指標，均上升1.7%。

政府補貼使能源價格仍呈下跌，但跌幅小於5月。耐久財與醫療費用也推高通膨。食品與飲料的預定漲價較一年前增加21.9%，企業也更願意把較高的投入成本轉嫁給消費者。日本大部分能源與相當比重的食品仰賴進口，日圓貶值與油價高企因此進一步增添壓力。

市場普遍預期日本央行7月31日將把政策利率維持在1%，並公布更新後的預測。後續決策將取決於匯率傳導與企業定價是否使通膨擴散到足以支持早於經濟學家偏好的12月時程升息。市場對10月升息的預期更為進取；若日本央行指引未能支持這項時程，市場仍有顯著調整空間。

新加坡在7月27日的政策檢討也面臨類似的輸入型通膨問題。18名經濟學家中有13名預期新加坡金融管理局維持匯率政策設定不變，4名預期提高政策區間的升值斜率，另有1名預期重新設定區間中點。6月核心通膨率為1.6%，處於金管局預測區間低端；但電價預定創紀錄上調17%，油價接近$100也提高延後傳導的風險。

國內經濟強勁，使耐心觀望的理由更為複雜。受AI相關需求支撐電子產品出口，新加坡第2季經濟成長5.7%，高於全年2%至4%的預測。維持政策不變可讓金管局觀察能源價格的滯後影響，但決策者仍須評估正向產出缺口與輸入成本是否需要日後採取更強行動。

## AI支出擴大信用市場的考驗

股市下跌使AI投資與固定收益供給之間的關聯更加鮮明。即使Google Cloud成長優於預期，Alphabet仍將2026年資本支出預測上調至最高$2,050億，股價下跌約7%。Tesla獲利不如預期，第2季AI與機器人支出達$58億，股價重挫15%。「科技七雄」合計市值蒸發約$7,970億。

市場擔心的並非支出停止，而是支出依然龐大，投資人卻要求看到更明確的回報證據。Meta、Microsoft、Amazon與Alphabet先前表示，今年AI支出合計最高可達$7,250億。在美國公債供給與殖利率本已偏高之際，若透過企業債、專案融資及私募市場為這波建設籌資，將增加另一項長天期債務供給來源。

一筆與Broadcom及Anthropic相關、規模$350億的融資案，顯示私人AI債務正走向更廣泛的市場。曾擔任配售代理的美國銀行、高盛與摩根士丹利，已開始交易其中一筆$240億分券的部分債務；報價顯示，債券賣價約為每$1面額100至100.5美分。

Apollo與Blackstone共同安排整體融資。借款人是一家特殊目的公司，負責購買Google與Broadcom開發的客製化晶片，再出租給Anthropic。資金動用後，部分債務可在Rule 144A市場交易，使合格買方擴及保險公司與共同基金等機構。這項架構把有合約支持的科技運算能力轉化為可交易信用資產，但投資人仍須承擔資產表現、租約持續性，以及AI需求能否延續的經濟風險。

這筆交易也凸顯私人信用與公開信用之間的界線日益模糊。Apollo正在建立私人發起資產的交易業務，截至第1季底已處理$150億。銀行居間及144A資格，可為最初在傳統聯貸市場之外安排的債務創造流動性；但這項流動性取決於投資人是否願意接受標的專案，以及風險集中於快速變化科技產業的事實。

BlackRock認為，美國公債殖利率偏高，如今可為後續損失提供較多緩衝。其季度展望估計，10年期殖利率還須再上升約70個基點，持有一年的總報酬才會轉負。若聯準會維持利率不變，美國公債指數預估報酬為6.4%；若降息50個基點，報酬為7.2%；若升息100個基點，報酬為2.5%；若經濟衰退並降息150個基點，報酬則為11.6%。

這些情境取決於政策路徑，並未消除相關不確定性。截至週三，美國公債指數今年已下跌0.7%，7月至今下跌0.9%。BlackRock認為市場定價比合理程度更偏鷹，但初領失業救濟數據、油價衝擊與7月會議的升息機率，仍使另一種緊縮情境具有現實意義。

在歐洲信用市場，即使企業債利差接近紀錄低點，BlackRock仍強調較高基礎殖利率帶來的收益。該公司認為公用事業、電信、基礎建設、醫療保健與銀行業的資產負債表具韌性，但汽車及化工業面臨較大壓力；對CCC級借款人，以及仍須依靠營運成長支撐資產負債表的企業則更為審慎。當整體殖利率偏高，卻幾乎沒有補償發行人個別信用惡化的風險時，這項區別愈來愈重要。

針對規模$1.3兆的美國擔保貸款憑證（CLO）市場，一項研究指出，海外政策與融資條件可經由另一條管道影響企業借款成本。UCLA的Shohini Kundu與華頓商學院的Amy Huber在工作論文中探討，日圓兌美元交叉貨幣基差如何影響日本銀行對AAA級CLO分券的需求，並透過這項需求影響新券利差與貸款市場融資。

日本證券化規則在2019年改變前，農林中央金庫占日本銀行CLO持有量的55%，是相對穩定的買方。更嚴格的資本及盡職調查規定削弱其主導地位後，買方對避險後的美元融資成本更為敏感。此後，基差每改善10個基點，新發行AAA級CLO利差約收窄22個基點；規則調整前，相同變化僅對應約3個基點的利差收窄。

日本央行自2023年底開始推動政策正常化後，這項關係再次改變。日本國內殖利率上升，降低銀行把日圓換成美元的誘因，使其CLO需求對邊際融資條件變化較不敏感。同樣是基差改善10個基點，後來只對應約15個基點的利差收窄，對發行量的影響也減弱。5年期日圓兌美元基差目前約為負0.29個百分點，是多年來負值最小的水準，而日本對CLO的需求仍然穩健。這項研究說明，日本央行政策與日本銀行的資產負債表容量，也是高槓桿美國企業融資成本的變數，不能把CLO需求視為純粹的美國國內因素。

壓力信用市場則出現較直接的法律進展。Dish Network取得法院附條件批准，可向債權人發送一項重整方案；該方案將削減數十億美元的衛星電視債務，並結束失敗的5G建設。法官Christopher Lopez要求提供更多資訊，並認為公司提議的時程過快而予以否決，改在10月初舉行確認方案的聽證會。

這項裁決並未批准重整方案本身。Crown Castle及American Tower等電信塔營運商主張，Dish正利用公司間債券債務，消除與終止5G建設相關的數十億美元損害賠償請求。Crown Castle表示，Dish積欠其超過$35億，但依提案每$1債權僅能收回1至2美分。另有超過1,000名曾出租場地設置Dish設備的業主，其債權也將受損。

這項方案獲得持有Dish DBS多數債券的投資機構支持，包括BlackRock、GoldenTree、摩根大通與Pimco。一個特別委員會正在調查可能針對第三方提出的請求權。下一階段的核心將同時包括回收率，以及支持方案的債券持有人、電信塔公司、房東與其他無擔保債權人之間如何分配價值。

Cellnex Telecom面對的則是仍在初步評估的策略交易選項。這家電信塔公司股價較2021年高點下跌約60%後，管理階層曾考慮私有化或合併。公司含債務的企業價值約為€370億，槓桿因而成為任何交易的重大障礙。先前與DigitalBridge及德國電信支持的財團進行的談判未超越初步階段，目前也未達成任何新交易。

相較之下，盧森堡是在沒有融資壓力的情況下，尋求小幅擴大投資人基礎。該國計畫明年1月發行€2.5億的3年期零售債券，為可負擔住宅籌資；此前一筆票息2.25%、規模€1.5億的國防債券在一天內售罄。盧森堡擁有AAA主權評等，債務低於GDP的30%。該國預期，在€265億的債務存量中，零售債券市場最終可達€10億，但會限制計畫規模，以免從銀行吸走過多存款。

## 後續市場意義

美國7月24日公布的新屋銷售，是下一項直接檢驗美國公債與房貸利率究竟帶來多少抑制作用的數據。30年期房貸平均利率已升至6.58%，10年期美國公債殖利率一個月上升18.4個基點。若住房需求疲弱，將顯示市場利率的傳導作用加深；若需求仍具韌性，聯準會便更缺乏理由淡化油價帶來的通膨風險。

7月27日公布的耐久財訂單初值，將檢驗企業投資是否仍強到足以支撐偏高的實質殖利率。10年期實質殖利率已升至2.424%，而初領失業救濟數據顯示裁員有限，因此這項區別相當重要。訂單穩健將強化目前融資成本尚未造成廣泛需求斷裂的看法；若訂單疲弱，近期利率上升對成長的代價就會更加明顯。

聯準會決策前，美國公債標售將帶來一連串需求考驗。2年期及5年期公債定於7月27日標售，7年期則在7月28日登場。前端標售將顯示，投資人如何為立即升息機率約35%及已完全反映的9月升息定價。在現券交易異常活躍、5年期殖利率上升4.9個基點後，7年期標售則將檢驗中段天期需求。

7月28至29日的FOMC會議仍是核心事件。市場必須區分能源成本的潛在傳導，以及通膨已實際擴散的證據。若聯準會按兵不動，焦點將轉向官員是否確認市場已完全反映的9月升息；若立即行動，則表示油價高於$100、就業穩健及通膨預期不確定性的組合，已足以縮短政策反應時程。

衝突發展的重要性可能不亞於會議措辭。荷莫茲海峽與紅海若持續同時受阻，能源、航運與保險成本將繼續承壓；可信的降溫則可能在這些成本擴散至更廣泛價格前，逆轉部分近期政策溢價。10年期損益兩平通膨率當日下降，因此下一階段利率走勢取決於油價上升是否開始推高實際測得的基礎通膨，或主要仍是提高實質利率與政策不確定性。

新加坡7月27日的決策與日本央行7月31日的會議，分別檢驗亞洲的輸入型通膨壓力。新加坡金管局必須在1.6%的核心通膨率、電價上調17%及第2季成長5.7%之間權衡。市場預期日本央行把利率維持在1%，但其預測及對日圓貶值傳導的說明，將決定10月升息是否仍比經濟學家偏好的12月時程更為可信。

歐洲最主要的未決條件是歐洲央行9月會議。在7週間隔期間，官員將取得新預測，以及更多通膨與經濟活動數據。若證據顯示能源成本正進入服務、商品或工資，將支持再升息25個基點；若基礎通膨持續受控、達成和平協議或經濟下滑加深，則會挑戰目前幾乎認定9月升息的市場定價。

AI企業財報與融資則是另一項長天期資金及信用市場容量的考驗。超大規模雲端業者若進一步提高支出，將擴大與主權借款人競逐長期資本的融資案供給。規模$350億的Broadcom-Anthropic融資案進入交易後，可觀察風險承擔範圍從原始私募配置擴大時，投資人是否仍願意以接近面額的價格評價晶片租約。現在的問題已不只是AI基礎設施能否取得融資，而是當這類融資在債券市場占比提高時，買方願意承擔多少資產負債表、專案與科技風險。

overall_summary.headline: 油價使聯準會7月升息成為可能，美國公債在跌勢中曲線趨平
overall_summary.session_narrative:
兩艘沙烏地阿拉伯油輪遇襲，使中東衝突在荷莫茲海峽之外開闢第2條活躍的航運戰線，美國公債因而延續跌勢。布蘭特原油上漲6.97%至$100.63，交換市場估計聯準會在7月28至29日會議升息25個基點的機率約為35%，高於一週前的約10%。初領失業救濟人數降至18.7萬人，創1969年以來最低，幾乎未顯示足以迫使決策者忽略能源衝擊的勞動市場惡化。

2年期與5年期殖利率均上升4.9個基點，分別至4.348%與4.453%；10年期上升3.8個基點至4.694%，30年期上升1.5個基點至5.161%。前端領跌使2s10s縮窄至34.6個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升5.7個基點，損益兩平通膨率卻下降1.9個基點，顯示投資人提高了預期政策與實質利率負擔，而非單純增加通膨補償。

全球市場均出現重新定價，但走勢並不一致。歐洲央行將存款利率維持在2.25%，同時保留9月行動空間；德國10年期公債殖利率收在約3.19%；中國公債則因成長轉弱及寬鬆預期而上漲。美國股市下跌、波動率上升，油價與殖利率走高，也加深市場對AI投資回報及融資需求的疑慮。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries extended their selloff on July 23 as attacks on two Saudi oil tankers opened a second active shipping front in the Middle East conflict, drove Brent above $100 a barrel and brought the possibility of a Federal Reserve rate increase closer to the July meeting. The move was led by policy-sensitive maturities: the 2-year and 5-year yields each rose 4.9 basis points, to 4.348% and 4.453%, while the 10-year increased 3.8 basis points to 4.694% and the 30-year added 1.5 basis points to 5.161%. The resulting bearish flattening took 2s10s down 1.1 basis points to 34.6 basis points and 2s30s down 3.4 basis points to 81.3 basis points.

The session combined a larger prospective energy shock with evidence that the U.S. labor market still gives the Fed room to concentrate on inflation. Initial jobless claims fell by 22,000 to 187,000 in the week through July 18, the lowest level since 1969 and well below the 210,000 median forecast. Swaps assigned roughly a 35% probability to a quarter-point increase at the July 28–29 meeting, up from about 10% a week earlier, and fully priced an increase by September.

The Treasury decomposition was more demanding than an inflation-only account. The 10-year real yield climbed 5.7 basis points to 2.424%, while the 10-year breakeven rate declined 1.9 basis points to 2.27%. Oil altered the near-term policy calculation, but investors also required a higher inflation-adjusted return as labor data remained firm and the economy continued to absorb large investment spending. The front-end-led flattening showed where the marginal policy adjustment was concentrated, while the 30-year yield’s continued hold above 5% preserved the separate pressure from fiscal and corporate supply.

Crude supplied the day’s defining shock. Brent gained 6.97% to $100.63, leaving it 19.47% higher over a week and 29.18% higher over a month. WTI rose 6.18% to $92.20. Houthi forces said they had attacked two Saudi tankers with missiles and drones in the Red Sea, following months in which disruption through the Strait of Hormuz had already impaired Gulf shipping. The attacks threatened the alternative route Saudi Arabia had relied upon to maintain exports, while Washington and Tehran remained unwilling to return to negotiations and President Donald Trump threatened a broader attack.

Risk assets supplied little offset to the rates selloff. The S&P 500 fell 1.21% and the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.87%, while the VIX rose 12.38% to 18.70. Alphabet’s larger capital-spending plan and Tesla’s earnings intensified a reassessment of AI investment at the same time that higher oil and yields weighed on valuations. The dollar index gained 0.29%, and gold fell 2.29% to $4,051.80 as higher real yields and prospective policy tightening outweighed geopolitical demand. Investment-grade and high-yield bond funds declined about 0.4%, while an emerging-market debt fund lost 0.59%, indicating pressure on traded credit assets without establishing a broad spread rupture.

The oil-driven repricing was global. The European Central Bank kept its deposit rate at 2.25%, yet President Christine Lagarde disclosed that some officials had considered an immediate increase and left September open. German 10-year yields reached a 15-year high before finishing near 3.19%. Turkey also held rates, but with effective funding still at 40% as officials waited to see whether energy costs interrupt disinflation. The common development was not simultaneous tightening; it was a reduction in the room to dismiss imported energy pressure while domestic inflation, growth and currency conditions remained different.

## Oil Brings the Fed Decision Forward

The attack on the Saudi tankers converted a prospective Red Sea threat into a realized disruption. Houthi forces said they fired missiles and drones at the vessels to enforce a blockade of Saudi ports, and a tanker master reported a strike southwest of Al Shuqaiq on the Saudi coast. The confrontation now encompasses both the Strait of Hormuz, the principal exit from the Persian Gulf, and the Red Sea route connected to the Suez Canal.

That second front matters because alternative infrastructure and shipping routes had limited the effect of impaired Hormuz traffic. Interference with Saudi cargoes in the Red Sea reduces the reliability of that buffer, adding risks to freight, insurance and delivery schedules even before any physical loss of production. Brent settled at $100.63, its first close above $100 in nearly two months, as global inventories had already been depleted by months of conflict.

The escalation also acquired a more explicit U.S. policy dimension. Trump said he would hold Iran responsible for further Houthi attacks and was close to deciding on a much larger strike. Neither Washington nor Tehran indicated that negotiations were imminent. The Treasury market therefore had to price not merely the day’s oil jump but the risk that a prolonged or broader conflict keeps energy costs high enough to affect goods, services, wages and inflation expectations.

Market pricing moved sharply toward an immediate Fed decision. Meeting-dated swaps put the probability of a July increase near 35%, compared with about 10% a week earlier, while at least one quarter-point move was fully priced by September. That was a substantial change so close to a meeting, particularly because Chair Kevin Warsh has provided less advance guidance than his predecessors. The absence of a clearly telegraphed decision has left investors more willing to assign weight to both outcomes.

Some rates investors regarded the July pricing as too aggressive. TD Securities strategist Gennadiy Goldberg argued that the Fed would probably want several more months of core-inflation evidence before resuming increases, even though a move later in the year carried significant risk. The distinction is important: oil has raised the probability of renewed tightening, but the market has not received evidence that an energy increase has already broadened into underlying inflation.

The claims report nevertheless weakened the case for treating the energy shock as the only consideration. Initial applications dropped to 187,000 from 209,000, against a 210,000 forecast, signaling that layoffs remained unusually limited. A labor market with little visible dismissal pressure gives policymakers more scope to respond to prospective inflation without immediately creating an obvious conflict with the employment side of their mandate.

The report was not an unqualified acceleration signal. The latest monthly employment figures had shown workers leaving the labor force, which can reduce claims without representing stronger labor demand. Even with that qualification, the weekly result offered no evidence of the broad deterioration that would force the Fed to look past a renewed energy shock.

Housing showed more clearly how high market yields are transmitting restraint. The average rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage rose for a third week, to 6.58% from 6.55%, although it remained below the 6.74% rate a year earlier. The increase followed the rebound in Treasury yields after a fragile ceasefire collapsed, reversing part of the financing-cost relief that had begun to support housing demand.

The day’s curve move reflected the tension between prospective inflation and existing restraint. The 2-year yield reached 4.348%, 20.6 basis points higher over a week, while the 10-year rose to 4.694%, up 14 basis points over the same period. The 30-year yield gained less on the day but stood 21.2 basis points higher over a month. Near-term policy risk drove the latest flattening; elevated term and real yields kept longer-duration financing restrictive even without an equally large daily move.

The real-yield increase was particularly notable. A 5.7-basis-point rise in the 10-year TIPS yield more than accounted for the 3.8-basis-point increase in the nominal 10-year yield because the breakeven declined. That configuration does not negate the oil catalyst. It indicates that the market responded to the shock partly by raising the expected policy and real-rate burden rather than simply adding inflation compensation.

Treasury activity expanded as the adjustment took place. FINRA recorded $1.158 trillion of par trading across 411,593 transactions, with total activity 12.2% higher than the previous session. Nominal-coupon volume rose 16.4% to $912.6 billion. Activity in maturities longer than 7 years and no more than 10 years increased 33.7% to $188.6 billion, while the 5- to 7-year sector rose 33.6% to $77.9 billion. The figures show unusually heavy two-way turnover in the sectors absorbing the repricing, without identifying whether customers were net buyers or sellers.

A late trade-policy action added another prospective price risk. The U.S. imposed tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on imports from about 60 economies after forced-labor investigations, with Japan and South Korea at the upper end of the range. Fuel, food and fertilizer were exempt. The exemptions limit the most direct overlap with the day’s energy shock, but the broader tariff wall leaves another channel through which input costs and supply chains can affect the inflation outlook.

## Europe Pauses Without Closing the Door

The ECB unanimously kept its deposit rate at 2.25%, its main refinancing rate at 2.40% and its marginal lending rate at 2.65%. Its asset-purchase and pandemic portfolios continued to decline without reinvestment of principal. The decision followed June’s quarter-point increase and preserved a meeting-by-meeting approach while officials assessed the duration and breadth of the energy shock.

The hold did not amount to a neutral signal. Lagarde said some governors had asked whether the ECB should raise rates immediately. She described the current setting as adequate while officials wait for incoming information, but emphasized that inflation risks were tilted upward and that a longer-lasting energy increase would be more likely to enter other prices and wages.

Officials were especially concerned about the interaction between oil and gas. Brent crossed $100 during Lagarde’s press conference, while European gas prices had also risen against a background of low inventories. The ECB asked its staff to conduct more detailed energy analysis for the September meeting, when policymakers will have new forecasts, 2 additional months of inflation data and further business surveys.

The immediate inflation evidence remained comparatively benign. June headline inflation slowed to 2.8% from 3.2% in May, and underlying price growth had stayed contained. Lagarde said there were no signs yet of second-round effects. The ECB nevertheless expects the accumulated energy rise and its pass-through to food, goods and services to keep inflation well above target through the first half of 2027.

That combination explains why September became the focal point rather than why the ECB acted in July. Officials familiar with the deliberations said another quarter-point increase would probably be needed unless the inflation outlook improved materially. They also stressed that no decision had been made and that a peace agreement or a more severe downturn could change the assessment.

German bonds had already repriced much of that risk. The 10-year Bund yield rose as high as 3.21%, its highest since 2011, before finishing around 3.19%, 2 basis points higher. Swaps treated a September increase as nearly certain and almost priced another move by year-end. The limited reaction to the decision itself showed that the market had anticipated the hold and was focused instead on energy and the conditional September path.

Supply remained a separate support for higher European yields. Germany’s defense and infrastructure programs require substantial borrowing, while the spending may also support activity sufficiently to strengthen the case for restrictive policy. The U.K. 10-year yield stood near 5.09%, with markets expecting 2 Bank of England increases by year-end and a third by the middle of 2027. European and U.K. rates had re-established a strong directional relationship with crude, even though individual central banks faced different inflation and growth conditions.

Turkey chose another restrictive hold. The central bank kept the 1-week repo rate at 37% for a fourth meeting, matching all 20 economist forecasts, and maintained the overnight lending rate at 40%. That overnight rate has served as the effective funding cost since the Iran war began, making the unchanged headline rate less accommodative than it appears.

The Turkish Monetary Policy Committee said the underlying inflation trend would rise temporarily in July as renewed geopolitical uncertainty pushed energy prices higher. Annual inflation had slowed to 32.1% in June, the first deceleration since the conflict began, but the central bank wanted to assess July data and the war before changing its rates path. The lira was little changed near 47.23 per dollar after the decision.

Policy expectations remain divided between the need to preserve disinflation and the possibility that the next move could eventually be an easing. BBVA strategist Tufan Comert did not expect a material reduction in effective funding costs before autumn, but judged that easing would remain the more likely next step if external risks receded and disinflation resumed after the anticipated July increase. Bloomberg Economics expected the 37% policy rate to remain in place through year-end and forecast inflation at 29.5% in December, above the central bank’s 26% projection.

Mexico presented a less acute inflation problem but still insufficient progress for renewed easing. Headline inflation slowed to 3.1% in the first half of July from 3.18% in June, matching forecasts and reaching its lowest level since 2020. Core inflation edged up to 3.95% from 3.94%, slightly above expectations, while services inflation eased to 4.36%.

Banxico had unanimously held its policy rate at 6.50% in late June and said maintaining that setting was appropriate. The latest headline decline supports the pause, but sticky core and services prices argue against an immediate cut. The bank expects headline and core inflation at 3.5% in Q4 and convergence to its 3% target in Q2 2027, while continuing to judge the risks around that path as tilted upward.

## Asian Duration Splits Between China and Japan

Chinese government bonds moved against the global selloff as weaker growth, falling equities and expectations of additional monetary support renewed demand for duration. The 30-year bond future reached its highest level since November, and open contracts rose 15% in a single session to a record. The cash 30-year yield had fallen to 2.21% from a March high of 2.39%, while the 10-year yield declined 2 basis points to 1.73%.

The rally followed weaker-than-expected Q2 growth and speculation that some banks could receive a deposit-rate reduction. Investors also anticipated possible stimulus at the Communist Party Politburo meeting. Those domestic expectations outweighed the global inflation shock that was pushing yields higher in the U.S., Europe and the U.K.

Auction demand reinforced the move. Bids at a 10-year government-bond sale reached 7.41 times the amount offered, the highest ratio in Bloomberg data extending to 2004. Flush liquidity, equity volatility and geopolitical uncertainty all supported demand, although the durability of the rally may depend on whether the 10-year yield can move below 1.70% without provoking concern from the People’s Bank of China.

Japan faced the opposite configuration: imported energy pressure, an exceptionally weak currency and a central bank already moving away from accommodation. The yen fell as low as 163.99 per dollar, its weakest in four decades. A Bloomberg survey found that 50% of 52 economists expected the BOJ’s next increase in December and 40% in October, while markets assigned an 83% probability to a move by October.

Economists were becoming more open to an earlier move even before the latest inflation release. Some 37% identified September as the earliest possible tightening date, up from 23% after the June meeting. At the same time, 59% saw Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s preference for monetary support as an obstacle to faster normalization, and 82% expected increases to proceed at roughly one every 6 months.

Fresh Japanese inflation figures released early Friday in Tokyo strengthened the case for additional tightening later in the year but came after the completed U.S. close. CPI excluding fresh food rose 1.6% in June from a year earlier, matching the median forecast and accelerating for the first time in 3 months. Overall inflation and a measure excluding fresh food and energy both rose 1.7%.

Energy prices still declined because of government subsidies, but by less than in May. Durable goods and medical-treatment fees also contributed to the increase. Planned food and beverage price increases rose 21.9% from a year earlier, while companies have become more willing to pass higher input costs to consumers. The yen’s decline and elevated oil prices add further pressure for an economy that imports most of its energy and much of its food.

The BOJ is widely expected to leave its 1% policy rate unchanged on July 31 and publish updated projections. The subsequent decision will depend on whether currency pass-through and corporate pricing broaden inflation enough to justify moving earlier than the December timetable favored by economists. The market’s more aggressive October expectation leaves room for a meaningful adjustment if the BOJ’s guidance does not validate that timing.

Singapore faces a related imported-inflation question at its July 27 review. Thirteen of 18 economists expected the Monetary Authority of Singapore to keep its exchange-rate settings unchanged, while 4 expected a steeper policy-band slope and one anticipated re-centering. Core inflation was 1.6% in June, at the lower end of the MAS forecast range, but electricity tariffs are scheduled to rise a record 17% and oil near $100 increases the risk of delayed pass-through.

Domestic strength complicates the case for patience. Singapore’s economy expanded 5.7% in Q2, above the full-year projection of 2% to 4%, as AI-related demand supported electronics exports. A hold would allow the MAS to observe the lagged energy effect, but it would also leave policymakers assessing whether a positive output gap and imported costs require stronger action later.

## AI Spending Expands the Credit-Market Test

The equity selloff sharpened the connection between AI investment and fixed-income supply. Alphabet raised its 2026 capital-spending forecast to as much as $205 billion even as Google Cloud growth exceeded expectations. Its shares fell about 7%, while Tesla dropped 15% after profit disappointed and spending on AI and robotics reached $5.8 billion in Q2. The Magnificent Seven group lost roughly $797 billion in market value.

The concern was not that spending had stopped; it was that spending remained large while investors demanded clearer evidence of returns. Meta, Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet had indicated combined AI expenditure of as much as $725 billion this year. Financing that buildout through corporate, project and private markets adds another source of long-duration debt at a time when Treasury supply and yields are already elevated.

A $35 billion financing package connected to Broadcom and Anthropic illustrated how private AI debt is migrating toward a broader market. Bank of America, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley began trading portions of a $24 billion tranche for which they had served as placement agents. Quotes showed bonds offered around 100 to 100.5 cents on the dollar.

Apollo arranged the overall package with Blackstone. The borrower is a special-purpose vehicle that buys custom chips developed by Google and Broadcom and leases them to Anthropic. Once drawn, portions of the debt can trade in the Rule 144A market, widening the eligible buyer base to institutions including insurers and mutual funds. The structure turns contracted technology capacity into tradable credit while leaving investors exposed to asset performance, lease durability and the economics of continuing AI demand.

The transaction also demonstrates the increasingly porous boundary between private and public credit. Apollo has been building a trading operation for privately originated assets and handled $15 billion through the end of Q1. Bank intermediation and 144A eligibility can create liquidity for debt initially arranged outside conventional syndicated markets, but that liquidity depends on investors accepting both the underlying project and its concentration in a rapidly changing technology sector.

BlackRock argued that elevated Treasury yields now provide more protection against further losses. Its quarterly outlook estimated that the 10-year yield would have to rise roughly another 70 basis points before a one-year holding produced a negative total return. It projected a 6.4% return for the Treasury index if the Fed stayed on hold, 7.2% with 50 basis points of easing, 2.5% with 100 basis points of increases and 11.6% in a recession accompanied by 150 basis points of easing.

Those scenarios depend on the policy path rather than resolving it. The Treasury index was already down 0.7% for the year and 0.9% in July through Wednesday. BlackRock judged market pricing more hawkish than warranted, while the claims report, oil shock and July meeting probability kept the alternative tightening scenario relevant.

In European credit, BlackRock emphasized income from higher underlying yields even though corporate spreads were near record tights. It cited resilient balance sheets in utilities, telecommunications, infrastructure, healthcare and banks, while identifying greater pressure in autos and chemicals. The firm was more cautious about CCC borrowers and companies that still needed operating growth to support their balance sheets. That distinction is increasingly important when a high all-in yield can coexist with little compensation for a deterioration in issuer-specific credit quality.

Research on the $1.3 trillion U.S. collateralized-loan-obligation market supplied another channel through which foreign policy and funding conditions affect corporate borrowing costs. A working paper by UCLA’s Shohini Kundu and Wharton’s Amy Huber examined how the yen-dollar cross-currency basis influences Japanese bank demand for AAA CLO tranches and, through that demand, new-issue spreads and loan-market financing.

Before Japanese securitization rules changed in 2019, Norinchukin Bank accounted for 55% of Japanese banks’ CLO holdings and acted as a relatively stable buyer. After stricter capital and due-diligence rules reduced its dominance, buyers became more sensitive to hedged dollar-funding costs. A 10-basis-point improvement in the basis then tightened new-issue AAA CLO spreads by roughly 22 basis points, compared with about 3 basis points before the regulatory change.

The relationship changed again after BOJ normalization began in late 2023. Higher domestic yields reduced the incentive for Japanese banks to swap yen into dollars, making their CLO demand less responsive to marginal funding changes. The same 10-basis-point basis improvement was associated with about 15 basis points of spread tightening, and its effect on issuance weakened. The 5-year yen-dollar basis now stands near minus 0.29 percentage point, its least negative level in years, while Japanese CLO demand remains firm. The finding identifies BOJ policy and Japanese balance-sheet capacity as variables in the financing cost of leveraged U.S. companies, rather than treating CLO demand as exclusively domestic.

Stressed credit produced a more immediate legal development. Dish Network received conditional court approval to send creditors a restructuring plan that would reduce billions of dollars of satellite-TV debt and wind down its failed 5G buildout. Judge Christopher Lopez required additional disclosure and rejected the company’s proposed timetable as too fast, setting an early-October hearing to consider confirmation.

The ruling did not approve the plan itself. Tower operators including Crown Castle and American Tower argue that Dish is using intercompany bond debt to eliminate billions of dollars of damage claims associated with the 5G wind-down. Crown Castle says it is owed more than $3.5 billion but would receive only 1 to 2 cents on the dollar under the proposal. More than 1,000 property owners who leased sites for Dish equipment also face impaired claims.

The plan is backed by investment firms holding most of Dish DBS’s bond debt, including BlackRock, GoldenTree, JPMorgan and Pimco. A special committee is investigating potential claims against third parties. The next stage will therefore turn on both recoveries and the allocation of value between supported bondholders, tower companies, landlords and other unsecured creditors.

Cellnex Telecom supplied a less advanced restructuring question. Executives have considered a take-private or a merger after the tower company’s shares fell roughly 60% from their 2021 peak. The company has an enterprise value near €37 billion including debt, making leverage a major obstacle to any transaction. Earlier talks with a group backed by DigitalBridge and Deutsche Telekom did not progress beyond an initial stage, and no new deal has been agreed.

Luxembourg, by contrast, is seeking a modest expansion of its investor base without funding pressure. It plans to sell €250 million of 3-year retail bonds in January to finance affordable housing after a €150 million defense issue carrying a 2.25% coupon sold out within a day. The sovereign has triple-A ratings and debt below 30% of GDP. It expects the retail market could eventually reach €1 billion within a €26.5 billion debt stock, while limiting the program to avoid drawing excessive deposits from banks.

## Forward Market Significance

The July 24 U.S. new-home-sales report is the next direct test of how much restraint is being delivered by Treasury and mortgage rates. The average 30-year mortgage rate has risen to 6.58%, while the 10-year Treasury yield is 18.4 basis points higher over a month. Weak housing demand would show more transmission from market rates; resilience would give the Fed less reason to discount the inflation risk created by oil.

Advance durable-goods orders on July 27 will test whether business investment remains strong enough to sustain elevated real yields. The distinction is important after the 10-year real yield rose to 2.424% and claims showed few layoffs. Firm orders would reinforce the view that current financing costs have not yet produced a broad demand break, while weakness would make the growth cost of the recent rates move more visible.

Treasury auctions add a sequence of demand tests before the Fed decision. The 2-year and 5-year notes are scheduled for July 27, followed by the 7-year note on July 28. The front-end sales will show how investors price a 35% probability of an immediate increase and a fully priced September move. The 7-year auction will test intermediate-duration demand after unusually heavy cash trading and a 4.9-basis-point rise in the 5-year yield.

The July 28–29 FOMC meeting remains the central event. The market must distinguish between a prospective energy pass-through and evidence that inflation has already broadened. A hold would shift attention to whether officials validate the fully priced September increase. An immediate move would confirm that the combination of oil above $100, firm employment and uncertainty about inflation expectations was sufficient to shorten the reaction horizon.

The path of the conflict may be at least as important as the meeting language. Sustained disruption across both Hormuz and the Red Sea would keep pressure on energy, shipping and insurance costs. A credible de-escalation could reverse some of the near-term policy premium before those costs enter broader prices. With the 10-year breakeven lower on the day, the next stage of the rates move depends on whether higher oil begins to lift measured underlying inflation or continues mainly to raise real-rate and policy uncertainty.

Singapore’s July 27 decision and the BOJ’s July 31 meeting provide separate tests of imported inflation in Asia. The MAS must weigh core inflation of 1.6% against a 17% electricity-tariff increase and 5.7% Q2 growth. The BOJ is expected to hold at 1%, but its projections and description of yen pass-through will determine whether an October increase remains more plausible than the December timing favored by economists.

The ECB’s September meeting is the principal unresolved European condition. Officials will receive new forecasts and additional inflation and activity data during the 7-week interval. Evidence that energy costs are entering services, goods or wages would support another quarter-point increase. Continued restraint in underlying inflation, a peace agreement or a deeper downturn would challenge a market that has treated a September move as nearly certain.

AI earnings and financing remain a separate duration and credit-capacity test. Further increases in hyperscaler spending would add to the pipeline competing with sovereign borrowers for long-term capital. Trading in the $35 billion Broadcom-Anthropic package will show whether investors continue to value its chip leases near par as exposure broadens beyond the original private placement. The relevant question is no longer merely whether AI infrastructure can obtain financing, but how much balance-sheet, project and technological risk buyers will accept as that financing becomes a larger part of the bond market.

section_summaries.summary: The Treasury selloff was led by policy-sensitive maturities after tanker attacks drove Brent above $100 and brought a July Fed increase into play. Claims at 187,000 gave policymakers room to focus on inflation, while higher real yields and lower breakevens showed that the adjustment extended beyond inflation compensation. Long yields remained elevated amid fiscal and corporate supply pressure, and weakness in equities and traded credit offered little offset.

section_summaries.section_title: Oil Brings the Fed Decision Forward
section_summaries.summary: Attacks on Saudi tankers turned the Red Sea threat into a realized disruption and weakened the alternative route that had buffered impaired Hormuz traffic. Markets raised the probability of a July Fed increase to about 35%, although some investors argued that underlying inflation evidence remained insufficient. Claims showed little dismissal pressure, mortgage rates rose to 6.58%, and heavy Treasury turnover accompanied a repricing driven more by real yields than by breakevens.

section_summaries.market_read: Bunds had largely priced the July hold; energy, fiscal supply and the conditional September path drove yields.
section_summaries.section_title: Europe Pauses Without Closing the Door
section_summaries.summary: The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.25%, but Lagarde said some officials considered an immediate increase and made September the focal point for new forecasts and energy pass-through. German 10-year yields finished near 3.19% as markets treated a September move as nearly certain. Turkey held its policy rate at 37% with effective funding at 40%, while softer Mexican headline inflation supported Banxico’s pause without resolving sticky core and services inflation.

section_summaries.market_read: Domestic easing expectations outweighed global inflation pressure in China, while imported costs tightened Japan’s trade-off.
section_summaries.next_check: BOJ guidance on July 31 will test whether October tightening remains more plausible than December.
section_summaries.section_title: Asian Duration Splits Between China and Japan
section_summaries.summary: Chinese government bonds rallied against the global selloff as weaker Q2 growth, equity losses and expectations of monetary support renewed demand for duration; exceptionally strong auction demand reinforced the move. Japan faced the opposite pressure from a four-decade-low yen, expensive oil and an expected path toward further BOJ tightening. Singapore’s July 27 review must balance subdued core inflation against a 17% electricity-tariff increase and 5.7% Q2 growth.

section_summaries.market_read: AI financing is becoming an additional source of long-duration supply as private structures migrate into tradable credit.
section_summaries.section_title: AI Spending Expands the Credit-Market Test
section_summaries.summary: Alphabet’s higher capital-spending plan and Tesla’s earnings intensified scrutiny of AI returns as major platforms contemplated as much as $725 billion of annual investment. The $35 billion Broadcom-Anthropic financing showed private AI debt moving toward tradable institutional credit, adding potential long-duration supply while exposing buyers to lease durability and technology risk. Dish separately received conditional approval to solicit its restructuring plan, leaving recoveries and value allocation unresolved.

Housing, durable-goods data and Treasury auctions will test whether elevated financing costs are restraining demand before the July 28–29 FOMC meeting. The central rates question is whether sustained disruption across Hormuz and the Red Sea broadens inflation or continues mainly to raise real-rate and policy uncertainty. Later tests include Asian policy guidance, the ECB’s September assessment of energy pass-through, and investors’ capacity to absorb expanding AI-related debt.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury curve flattens in selloff as oil brings a July Fed increase into play
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries extended their selloff after attacks on two Saudi tankers opened a second active shipping front alongside the Strait of Hormuz. Brent rose 6.97% to $100.63, and swaps lifted the probability of a quarter-point Fed increase at the July 28–29 meeting to roughly 35% from about 10% a week earlier. Initial jobless claims fell to 187,000, the lowest since 1969, leaving little evidence of labor-market deterioration that would force policymakers to look past the energy shock.

The 2-year and 5-year yields each rose 4.9 basis points, to 4.348% and 4.453%, while the 10-year increased 3.8 basis points to 4.694% and the 30-year added 1.5 basis points to 5.161%. The front-end-led move flattened 2s10s to 34.6 basis points. A 5.7-basis-point rise in the 10-year real yield, alongside a 1.9-basis-point decline in the breakeven rate, showed that investors raised the expected policy and real-rate burden rather than simply adding inflation compensation.

The repricing was global but uneven. The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.25% while leaving September open, German 10-year yields finished near 3.19%, and Chinese government bonds rallied on weaker growth and easing expectations. U.S. equities fell and volatility rose as higher oil and yields compounded concern about the returns and financing demands associated with AI investment.
